transcript.statement: Sustainability is crucial for the Autonomous Driving System not just for regulatory compliance but also for reducing environmental impacts. GRN-01 ensures energy efficiency during operation, while GRN-02 promotes renewable energy use, reducing carbon emissions. GRN-03 addresses lifecycle assessments to minimize resource impacts. GRN-04 improves energy recovery, and GRN-05 aims for a significant reduction in emissions. GRN-06 optimizes routing for energy savings, and GRN-07 focuses on minimizing energy usage during failures. These requirements collectively support a sustainable operational framework.

transcript.statement: In the Autonomous Driving System, security and privacy are paramount to protect user data and ensure system integrity. TRU-01 mandates end-to-end data encryption, safeguarding personal information. TRU-02 establishes role-based access control, ensuring that users only access data necessary for their roles. TRU-03 emphasizes auditability by logging access and modifications, crucial for accountability. TRU-04 incorporates data anonymization to protect user identities. TRU-05 requires regular security audits to identify vulnerabilities. TRU-06 ensures secure remote software updates to mitigate malware risks. Finally, TRU-07 informs users about data collection, enhancing trust. These requirements collectively protect user data while supporting compliance with safety and operational standards.

conflicts_raised.description: Implementing strong data encryption (TRU-01) may increase processing overhead, potentially conflicting with the requirement to maintain a jerk value below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation (EFF-02).

Secure remote software updates (TRU-06) may introduce delays that conflict with the requirement to handle non-convex obstacle constraints quickly (EFF-06), potentially impacting system responsiveness.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is critical for the Autonomous Driving System, ensuring optimal travel time while maintaining passenger comfort and safety. EFF-01 focuses on reducing travel time significantly, enhancing overall system efficiency. EFF-02 ensures jerk is kept below limits during normal operations for comfort. EFF-03 emphasizes executing Minimal Risk Maneuvers quickly while balancing safety and performance. EFF-04 guarantees real-time monitoring of ODD compliance. EFF-05 aims for a high success rate in speed profile generation, while EFF-06 ensures rapid obstacle constraint handling. Lastly, EFF-07 prioritizes smoothness during emergencies to provide a safe transition. Together, these requirements optimize system performance while addressing safety concerns.

transcript.statement: Ethical considerations and compliance with regulations are paramount for the Autonomous Driving System. RES-01 ensures adherence to the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all times, which is fundamental for public safety. RES-02 establishes a multi-layer safety architecture for active monitoring and response to failures, reinforcing accountability. RES-03 mandates timely execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers, crucial for passenger safety. RES-04 and RES-05 ensure continuous monitoring and human takeover capability, essential for compliance. RES-06 prioritizes safety over comfort during emergencies, while RES-07 focuses on documenting safety decisions for accountability. These requirements collectively ensure ethical responsibility and compliance.

requirements.text: The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms to ensure collision protection and fail-safe operations.

The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures, ensuring safety while allowing a controlled 10% increase in energy consumption if safety protocols are maintained.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue a human takeover request when boundaries are approached.
The system shall minimize jerk to less than 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation, while ensuring safety protocols during critical maneuvers.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints ($kappa$) to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints with a response time of under 50 milliseconds.
The system shall ensure strong data protection protocols remain intact during critical maneuvers while allowing slight processing overhead.
The system shall document safety and compliance-related decisions for accountability and regulatory purposes.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures while allowing a 10% increase in energy consumption.

Energy minimization strategies are secondary to executing Minimal Risk Maneuvers.

The tension between safety and comfort during emergencies remains unresolved.
